A.explanation: With $L = 3\lambda/4 = 0.60\text{ m}$, $\lambda = 0.80\text{ m}$ and $f = v/\lambda = 340/0.80 \approx 430\text{ Hz}$.

B.explanation: Gives $v/L = 340/0.60 \approx 570\text{ Hz}$, which wrongly assumes one full wavelength fits in the 60 cm tube.

C.explanation: Gives $340/0.40 = 850\text{ Hz}$, which treats the 60 cm as $1.5\lambda$ as for a pipe open at both ends.

D.explanation: Gives $340/0.20 = 1700\text{ Hz}$, which treats the 60 cm as $3\lambda$ and miscounts node to antinode spacings.

hints: Notice the tube is open at the loudspeaker end and closed at the bottom, so there must be an antinode at the top and a node at the bottom.
Count along the 60 cm diagram: antinode-node-antinode-node uses three node-to-antinode gaps, and each gap is $\lambda/4$.
Use $L = 3\lambda/4$ to find $\lambda$ from $0.60\text{ m}$, then use $f = v/\lambda$ with $v = 340\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: Identify the end conditions from the diagram: open top at the loudspeaker is a displacement antinode, closed bottom is a displacement node.
Count the pattern stated as two nodes and two antinodes: going down it is antinode, node, antinode, node.
Recall the spacing rule: antinode to next node is $\lambda/4$, so three such intervals fit in the tube length.
Set $L = 3\lambda/4$ with $L = 60\text{ cm} = 0.60\text{ m}$, so $\lambda = 4L/3 = 4(0.60)/3 = 0.80\text{ m}$.
Apply the wave equation $v = f\lambda$, so $f = v/\lambda = 340/0.80 = 425\text{ Hz}$.
Round to the given precision, about $430\text{ Hz}$. This is option A.
